title: A laboratory for decisions about healthcare AI
subtitle: Learn the project’s scientific purpose, the chain from assumptions to outcomes, and how to read this book critically.
objectives: Explain why predictive accuracy alone does not determine deployment value.
Separate mathematical results, modeling choices, code behavior and empirical evidence.
Locate the scenario, experiment and review layers for a claim.
body:
## The central question A model can identify risk accurately and still make a service worse. Staff may have no time to act. An alert may arrive after the useful treatment window. A new workflow may duplicate existing care or displace a patient who would otherwise have been helped. Conversely, a modest predictor can support useful action when the intervention is effective, timely and inexpensive. The Healthcare Intervention Simulation SDK is a Python laboratory for studying this complete chain. It generates a population, evolves its circumstances through discrete time, produces model scores, applies a specified policy, and records outcomes. A branched simulation can propagate a comparison world without deployment of the model-driven intervention. Experiments vary assumptions and evaluate what those assumptions imply. The intended output is an argument about a decision: which mechanisms make a proposed deployment promising, fragile, harmful or hard to evaluate? The output is conditional on the constructed world. It is not a clinical trial, a substitute for local operational knowledge, or evidence that synthetic patients represent a particular hospital. ## Four kinds of statements
Mathematical resultA variance identity follows from definitions under its stated conditions. It does not need a hospital dataset.
Modeling assumptionAn intervention reduces risk by a configured amount. The simulation uses this claim; it does not establish it.
Implemented behaviorThe engine calls the scenario’s methods in a particular order. This is checked against source and tests.
Empirical illustrationA specific experiment produced a particular result. Its seed set, configuration and source identity delimit the claim.
These distinctions are the book’s organizing discipline. Equations are accompanied by their assumptions. Code excerpts show the implementation they explain. Worked examples are invented teaching examples unless explicitly identified as retained project evidence. A review question asks what evidence would justify moving from a modeled mechanism to an operational conclusion. For example, “probabilities sum to one” is an accounting property. “This population has 30% true malnutrition” is a model input unless independently justified. “The queue respects eight daily assessments” is a code behavior to test. “The ranked policy reduced missed diagnoses in three runs” is limited experimental evidence. Combining all four into “the intervention is validated” loses the distinctions needed for review. ## A first calculation before simulation Suppose an invented service sees 10,000 eligible encounters each year. Without intervention, 5% have an event. A predictor reaches 80% of those who would have an event; staff act on half the useful alerts; timely treatment prevents one quarter of otherwise occurring events. Under this deliberately simple, nonoverlapping, no-displacement model: ```math B=N\pi\,\mathrm{Se}\,a\,e ``` The expected benefit is 10,000 × 0.05 × 0.80 × 0.50 × 0.25 = **50 events averted**. Here N is eligible volume, π is the untreated event probability over the stated horizon, Se is sensitivity to those events, a is action probability conditional on a useful alert, and e is prevention probability conditional on action. The conditional meanings matter; multiplying unrelated marginal averages generally does not reproduce the joint probability. This is a useful first pass. It does not account for false-positive work, unequal treatment effects, repeated alerts, changing risk, delay, shared capacity or substitution for usual care. If specificity were 90%, the same operating point would also generate 950 false-positive alerts alongside 400 true-positive alerts. Fifty prevented events cannot be judged without the workload and consequences associated with those 1,350 alerts. Simulation is warranted when those interactions change the decision. It should add a mechanism that matters, not merely turn simple arithmetic into an elaborate animation. In particular, one can build useful analytical models of score distributions too; the repository’s preferred controlled-model workflow is an engineering convention, not a theorem that every ranking question requires this SDK. ## The project in layers | Layer | Main responsibility | Reviewer’s question | |---|---|---| | `core/` | Time orchestration, scenario interface, random streams and result containers | Is the experiment executed in the intended order without branch contamination? | | `population/` | Risk heterogeneity and temporal building blocks | Do distribution parameters and time units have the intended meaning? | | `ml/` | Generate scores or labels with controlled statistical properties | Which population, target and metric were actually calibrated? | | `scenarios/` | Clinical or operational mechanisms, eligibility, queues and outcomes | Does this represent the proposed and usual-care workflows? | | `experiments/` | Analysis, lifecycle, uncertainty, traces and review evidence | Are estimates, provenance and evidence requirements complete? | | `tests/`, `scripts/`, `docs/` | Executable checks, structural guards and human explanation | Which failure would each check detect, and what remains untested? | The engine treats state as an opaque object. A scenario may use a matrix, dataclasses or dictionaries. The five required behaviors are `create_population`, `step`, `predict`, `intervene` and `measure`. Optional helpers such as `clone_state` support the contract without adding another required clinical phase. This abstraction keeps scheduling generic while leaving responsibility for clinical meaning inside each scenario. A prediction object is not the entire intervention. The scenario decides eligibility, capacity, timing and action. An outcome object is not automatically an incident event count: its semantics are scenario-specific. The data chapter explains why that distinction is essential before fitting an estimator. ## What is implemented and what is aspirational The repository includes working scenarios for stroke prevention, appointment operations, retention, sepsis and malnutrition, plus paper-inspired implementations. These share infrastructure but differ in fidelity, calibration, workflow detail and validation maturity. A directory named after a published study does not certify that its code reproduces the study’s design. Chapter 13 gives the source-level atlas. The review-packet implementation adds traceable claims, evidence statuses, source/configuration/model identities, case walkthroughs and separate role views. It makes review more specific. It cannot supply a clinical reviewer’s judgment, repair a missing validation dataset, or make an incomplete statistical design applicable to a different deployment. This edition documents the locally implemented state at the displayed baseline and content hashes. Some relevant changes are not committed. A Git revision alone is therefore insufficient to identify the manuscript’s code snapshot. The evidence appendix records file-level hashes; the build and quality report describe the checks on this documentation. External scientific peer review remains pending. ## How to study the book Clinical and operational readers can begin here, then study decisions and capacity, the malnutrition example, and the review chapter. Quantitative readers should follow probability through causal comparisons and Monte Carlo error before reading the inference chapters. Engineers can connect the state contract and random streams to result semantics and verification, then use the worked numerical exercises as independent reference cases. The interactive labs are small teaching calculators. They do not execute the production simulator and do not modify project configurations. Their visible assumptions are intentionally narrower than a full scenario. Every lab presents numerical results as text as well as a chart, so the visual should make a quantity easier to understand without becoming its only representation. A productive review proceeds from a claim to an estimand, then to its assumptions, implementation, experiment, uncertainty and decision consequence. That sequence is more demanding than checking whether a notebook runs. It is also the route by which a simulation can become an inspectable scientific argument.

code_refs.claim: Defines the five required methods and optional state helpers.
Persists experiment evidence and registration through the common lifecycle.

review_questions: What decision would change because of this simulation?
Which inputs are measured locally, inferred from external evidence, or hypothetical?
What does the proposed policy change besides prediction?

exercises.question: In the first-pass example, staff act on only 10% of useful alerts. What happens to expected benefit?
exercises.answer: It falls from 50 to 10 events averted, if all other conditional probabilities and the no-displacement assumptions remain valid.

exercises.question: Why does a successful software test not establish treatment efficacy?
exercises.answer: A test can check that the configured effect is applied correctly. Whether that effect is realistic requires independent evidence about the intervention.
